status: DESIGNED EXERCISES — NOT EXECUTED. These are proposed preparation drills, not passing tests, implemented features or new qualification evidence.

drills.title: Interrupted retrieval keeps its original turn
drills.prompt: DESIGNED EXERCISE — NOT EXECUTED. A permitted retrieval for turn A stalls. The user interrupts, starts turn B and changes the request. A's lookup later returns valid historical evidence. Design the harness, ownership and assertions before implementing the adapter.
approach: Freeze a synthetic source, trusted account binding, turn A identity and bounded retrieval budget. Use an explicit barrier to hold the source read; record its actual task or offloaded I/O owner.

Advance to turn B and a distinct generation. Exercise both cooperative cancellation and a lookup that completes after the waiter stops. Release A's barrier without changing its retained source binding.
Observe incorporation, emitted output, tool calls and resource settlement independently. Run a current turn that should succeed so rejecting stale data cannot conceal a stalled system.
assertions: Late A output is never silently rebound into B. Any intentional reuse requires B's own permission and freshness decision; historical observations retain their original source and time.
Neither an interrupted response nor a late retrieval creates confirmation, supplier effects or another accepted user operation.
Pending/active resources stay bounded, and capacity is released only under the actual operation's settlement contract.
Authorized current work still completes, with explicit pending/no-source behavior when the chosen retrieval budget expires.
drills.trap: Cancelling the awaiter and immediately freeing capacity can hide live I/O; injecting into the current session can silently retarget old evidence.

drills.title: Lose the RPC reply after acceptance
drills.prompt: DESIGNED EXERCISE — NOT EXECUTED. A browser submits a permitted command through a proposed RPC adapter. The authority commits it, then the response is lost. Design reconnection and recovery without silently issuing another business operation.
approach: Choose a receipt-backed idempotent submit, not the revision-only CAS API. Freeze a synthetic scoped request and command identity; hold the RPC reply after committed acceptance.
Drop the response and retire the old browser lifecycle. Reconnect under a valid current grant, retaining the frozen original request rather than manufacturing a new key.
Reconcile through the authority's supported original-identity contract. Exercise exact replay, changed-body conflict, wrong-account disclosure and unavailable lookup as separate cases.
assertions: One original accepted operation and its receipt remain; retries of the same command do not add another logical booking.
A changed body cannot reuse the identity, and unauthorized recovery cannot read the retained result.
The UI reports pending/unknown honestly until supported evidence resolves it; a missed topic/card is not proof of business failure.
No supplier mutation occurs merely because transport timed out, a room changed or an RPC handler was invoked again.
drills.trap: An RPC library request ID is not automatically a retained business command key. A timeout does not prove the handler never committed.

drills.title: The transfer target never answers
drills.prompt: DESIGNED EXERCISE — NOT EXECUTED. A caller requests a human. In a proposed warm-transfer workflow the consultation dial times out, followed by a late answer event. Design the fallback and resource ownership without placing real calls.
approach: Model caller hold, permitted destination, consultation dial, briefing, merge and cleanup as explicit states. Use a scripted transport peer and bounded ringing/control budgets.
Hold the target answer behind a barrier, let the caller-facing wait expire, then deliver the late event. Repeat with caller hangup before answer.
Track original caller/target identities and owned tasks or remote legs. Separate a simulated state-machine check from the future real SIP/media/consultation-privacy gate.
assertions: The caller receives a truthful alternative rather than indefinite hold or a claimed successful human handoff.
A late event cannot merge an orphaned target, the wrong caller or a retired consultation.
Private briefing content never appears on the caller's output path before the intended merge.
Cleanup retains unresolved ownership and observes supported closure; local timeout is not proof that the remote call leg stopped.
drills.trap: Provider answer or successful forwarding can mean voicemail or an IVR. A scripted peer cannot qualify actual SIP behavior, audio privacy or human acceptance.

drills.title: The judge improves while an invariant fails
drills.prompt: DESIGNED EXERCISE — NOT EXECUTED. Candidate B sounds more helpful and receives a higher mean judge score than baseline A, but one scenario repeats a business effect. Design the promotion decision and retained evaluation evidence.
approach: Freeze synthetic scenarios, prompt/model/tool versions, authorized commands, expected hard invariants, judge rubric and judge version. Include refusal, ambiguity, unknown ACK and interruption.

Compare the same scenarios and declared repetitions. Use synthetic supplier/authority records for execution truth; keep language-quality scoring and independent deterministic checks as separate outputs.
Review a held-out human-labeled sample and judge disagreements. Record candidate differences, failures and missing observations before deciding whether further investigation or redesign is needed.
assertions: The repeated effect blocks promotion independently of average tone, relevance or judge score.
A model's claim that a tool succeeded is never the independent supplier or authority oracle.
Skipped, timed-out and unobserved required checks do not become passes or disappear from the denominator.
Any baseline/rubric update is intentional and reviewed; the old manifest and reason for change remain inspectable.
drills.trap: A single blended score can reward fluent false confirmations. Do not erase a hard failure by averaging it with many easy conversational successes.

field_guides.title: Choose the abstraction by the state it owns
rows: A session persona is not business consent.
Validate scope, arguments and effects at runtime.
Focused conversational collection returning a value
Await the pinned task API; annotations do not validate collected data. [A01]
Revision of a collected answer cannot undo a committed external effect. [A01]
Related Python task lifetimes and failure propagation
Process-local cancellation is not remote business cancellation. [PY]
A checkpoint or tool schema does not replace exact confirmation or original receipts. [A19]
Accepted obligations, issued execution and recovery
Keep one durable execution owner and original identities.

field_guides.title: Choose the LiveKit data API by its evidence
rows: Application/business authorization still needs trusted server bindings. [A09]
Handler timeout is not proof of noncommit; preserve the business identity. [A11]
Low-frequency state for room participants and late joiners
A mutable self-asserted value is not a permission or durable receipt. [A10]
Visible text is not a retained case or confirmed business effect. [L8]
Read completion/failure and declared/actual bytes need checking; not an unlimited inbox. [B07]
Reliable retransmission does not guarantee durable acceptance or actuator execution. [W6]
A transport ACK cannot substitute for its explicit retained contract.

field_guides.title: Freeze the voice experiment before comparing stacks
rows: Languages, accents, noise, pauses and interruptions
Pipeline, supported realtime or a named hybrid
Plugin/model versions, turn authority and fallback policy.
A stable session/cohort or explicit alternative
Speech end to first rendered audio, plus breakdowns
Clock limits, distribution, failures and sample count. [L12]
Entity errors, turn quality and useful task completion
Hard invariants separately from calibrated judge scores. [A17]
Actual dated billing quantities and unsuccessful work
Usage units, retries, hosting/transport and useful resolutions.
Queue age, saturation, rejection and owned cleanup.
One measured workload and selected mode
No universal latency, production capacity or price winner.
